arxiv-1811-05283.title: A priori and a posteriori error estimation for finite element approximation of advection-diffusion-reaction equation with spatially variable coefficients Thanks: chowdhurymanisha8@gmail.com
arxiv-1811-05283.creator: Prof. B.V. Rathish Kumar
arxiv-1811-05283.description: Abstract This paper presents a study of finite element error estimation of advection-diffusion-reaction equation with spatially variable coefficients. We have derived a priori and a posteriori errors in both energy and L 2 L_{2} norm. We have used residual-based a posteriori error estimator. Numerical results are also presented to verify our theoretical approach.

arxiv-2206-00614.creator: Ezechukwu I. Nwokedi, Rasneer S. Bains, Luc Bidaut, Xujiong Ye, Sara Wells, James M. Brown
arxiv-2206-00614.description: Abstract This paper presents a spatiotemporal deep learning approach for mouse behavioural classification in the home-cage. arxiv-2308-05320.title: Generating Transferable and Stealthy Adversarial Patch via Attention-guided Adversarial Inpainting
arxiv-2308-05320.creator: Yanjie Li, Mingxing Duan, Xuelong Dai, Bin Xiao 1. Computing Department, Hong Kong Polytechnic University2. School of Information Science and Engineering, Hunan University yanjie.li@connect.polyu.hk , xuelong.dai@connect.polyu.hk , duanmingxing@hnu.edu.cn , b.xiao@polyu.edu.hk
arxiv-2308-05320.description: Abstract Adversarial patch attacks can fool the face recognition (FR) models via small patches. However, previous adversarial patch attacks often result in unnatural patterns that are easily noticeable. Generating transferable and stealthy adversarial patches that can efficiently deceive the black-box FR models while having good camouflage is challenging because of the huge stylistic difference between the source and target images.

arxiv-2312-10297.title: Shedding Light on Software Engineering-specific Metaphors and Idioms Conference: 46th International Conference on Software Engineering; April 2024; Lisbon, Portugal

arxiv-2312-10297.description: Abstract . Use of figurative language, such as metaphors and idioms, is common in our daily-life communications, and it can also be found in Software Engineering (SE) channels, such as comments on GitHub. Automatically interpreting figurative language is a challenging task, even with modern Large Language Models (LLMs), as it often involves subtle nuances.

arxiv-2506-17356.description: Abstract We explore the automatic generation of interactive, scenario-based lessons designed to train novice human tutors who teach middle school mathematics online. Employing prompt engineering through a Retrieval-Augmented Generation approach with GPT-4o, we developed a system capable of creating structured tutor training lessons.

pmc-11225458.creator: Charles E Anyanechi, Birch D Saheeb
pmc-11225458.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). pmc-11592512.title: DNA Gene’s Basic Structure as a Nonperturbative Circuit Quantum Electrodynamics: Is RNA Polymerase II the Quantum Bus of Transcription?
pmc-11592512.creator: Raul Riera Aroche, Yveth M. Ortiz García, Esli C. Sánchez Moreno, José S. Enriquez Cervantes, Andrea C. Machado Sulbaran, Annie Riera Leal
pmc-11592512.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Previously, we described that Adenine, Thymine, Cytosine, and Guanine nucleobases were superconductors in a quantum superposition of phases on each side of the central hydrogen bond acting as a Josephson Junction. Genomic DNA has two strands wrapped helically around one another, but during transcription, they are separated by the RNA polymerase II to form a molecular condensate called the transcription bubble. Successive steps involve the bubble translocation along the gene body.

pmc-13200956.title: Association between C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index and atrial fibrillation recurrence: A retrospective cohort study
pmc-13200956.creator: Xiaojian Zhang, Yanping Yin, Qingru Zhu, Sixiang Jia, Weili Ge, Shudong Xia
pmc-13200956.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index reflects the body’s inflammatory, nutritional, and immune status, and has been shown to correlate with cancer prognosis. However, its impact on atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation outcomes remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed 1042 AF patients who underwent catheter-based radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) at 2 tertiary hospitals in China: The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine and Taizhou Hospital of Zhejiang Province. Each patient was followed for at least 3 months.

pmc-13631930.title: SCONE: a subset-contrastive method for multi-omics network embedding
pmc-13631930.creator: Pedro Henrique da Costa Avelar, Jonathan Cardoso-Silva, Min Wu, Sophia Tsoka
pmc-13631930.description: Network-based analyses of omics data are widely used and, while many of these methods have been adapted to single-cell scenarios, they often remain memory- and space-intensive. As a result, they are better suited to batch data or smaller datasets. Furthermore, the application of network-based methods in multi-omics often relies on similarity-based networks, which lack structurally discrete topologies.
